question.text:
CASE STUDY (continued): Priya wants to maximize her operational efficiency. She has clients investing across 8 different AMCs and is looking for a platform that allows consolidated transaction processing. She also wants to leverage her location in Lucknow (a B30 city) for better commissions.
Question 40: Per the current NISM V-A workbook, which combination of platform choice and B-30 strategy would best serve Priya's needs?

answer.text: Use NSE NMF II for all transactions because it provides settlement guarantee, and claim B-30 incentive for all existing investors regardless of city of residence

Use MF Utilities (MFU) for consolidated multi-AMC transactions, and focus on onboarding new individual investors from Lucknow and surrounding B-30 cities (and women investors), so as to benefit from additional commission/incentives as specified by SEBI from time to time
Use individual AMC websites for each of the 8 AMCs to maintain direct relationships, and register her Mumbai office address to avoid B-30 classification
Use BSE StAR MF exclusively because it offers the highest commission rates, and the B-30 incentive applies automatically to all transactions processed from any B-30 city

explanation.text: The Logic: MFU is the right operational choice for Priya's multi-AMC distribution because it enables consolidated processing across all 8 AMCs using CAN, Common Transaction Form, and consolidated payment. For the B-30 strategy, the current NISM V-A workbook describes additional commission/incentives for onboarding new individual investors from B-30 cities and women investors, as specified by SEBI from time to time — replacing the older fixed "additional 30 bps TER" framing. The Trap: Option A incorrectly assigns settlement guarantee to NSE NMF II for MF transactions and misapplies the B-30 rule. Option C suggests using 8 separate AMC websites — the opposite of operational efficiency — and a fake address, which is unethical. Option D claims platforms determine commission rates (AMCs do) and oversimplifies the B-30 incentive. Cross-Exam Context: The question integrates transaction channels (MFU vs. exchange platforms vs. AMC direct), the revised B-30/women-investor incentive framework, settlement-guarantee scope, and ethical conduct — all tested in NISM V-A.
